Installation & Setup

1. System Requirements
RequirementDetails
JDKOracle JDK 11/17 or OpenJDK 11/17
OSLinux, macOS 10.6+, Windows XP+
RAMMinimum 1 GB (production: depends on dataset size)
NetworkNo restrictions (10G recommended for production)
2. Using Binary Distribution
  • Download the binary package from Apache Ignite Downloads;
  • Unzip and set the IGNITE_HOME environment variable: 
    # Unzip
unzip apache-ignite-2.17.0-bin.zip

# Set IGNITE_HOME
export IGNITE_HOME=/path/to/apache-ignite-2.17.0-bin

# Start a node
$IGNITE_HOME/bin/ignite.sh
  • The default configuration starts a server node with TCP/IP discovery on localhost;
3. Using Maven
  • Add Ignite as a dependency in your pom.xml: 
    <properties>
    <ignite.version>2.17.0</ignite.version>
</properties>

<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.apache.ignite</groupId>
        <artifactId>ignite-core</artifactId>
        <version>${ignite.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.apache.ignite</groupId>
        <artifactId>ignite-spring</artifactId>
        <version>${ignite.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.apache.ignite</groupId>
        <artifactId>ignite-indexing</artifactId>
        <version>${ignite.version}</version>
    </dependency>
</dependencies>
  • ignite-core — core functionality;
  • ignite-spring — Spring XML-based configuration support;
  • ignite-indexing — SQL indexing and querying support;
4. Using Docker
  • # Pull and run the latest Ignite image
docker run -d \
  --name ignite-node \
  -p 10800:10800 \
  -p 47100:47100 \
  -p 47500:47500 \
  apacheignite/ignite:2.17.0

# Port 10800 — thin client connections
# Port 47100 — node communication
# Port 47500 — node discovery
5. Starting a Node Programmatically
  • // Minimal embedded node
IgniteConfiguration cfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
cfg.setClientMode(false); // server mode (default)

try (Ignite ignite = Ignition.start(cfg)) {
    System.out.println("Node started: " + ignite.name());
}
  • Ignite will automatically discover other nodes on the same network using multicast (default TCP/IP discovery with multicast IP finder);
6. Configuration Approaches
  • Programmatic (Java) — configure using IgniteConfiguration objects in Java code;
  • Spring XML — define beans in an XML file; pass the file path to Ignition.start("config.xml") or to ignite.sh;
  • Spring Boot — use the ignite-spring-boot-autoconfigure module for auto-configuration;
7. Work Directory
  • Ignite uses a work directory to store persistence data, index files, metadata, and logs;
  • Default: $IGNITE_HOME/work (if IGNITE_HOME is set) or ./ignite/work;
  • Override with: 
    IgniteConfiguration cfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
cfg.setWorkDirectory("/path/to/work/directory");
